title: Critic clues: what helps a small critic
subtitle: A small model reviews each compiled Reward Machine against the task. The compiler can add short, exact clues to the critic's prompt. This page shows which clues helped, which did not, and how much.

blocks.title: In plain words
blocks.text: The critic is a small model (`glm-5.3-flash`). It often accepts a wrong clause set. The compiler knows things the critic has to guess: what each clause means in plain words, and which hard clause adds nothing. Putting those facts in the prompt makes the critic catch more wrong sets. Three clues were kept. Nine other ideas were noise and were dropped.

items: **Critic set.** 38 items: 28 wrong clause sets with 41 labelled defects, 10 right ones. The critic reads one set at a time; a judge model says which defects its feedback names. Before: 6 runs per item (main code, no clues). After: one run per item (version v3 full).

**Pipeline.** 46 task cards through the full generate, compile, review loop (generator `deepseek-v4.1-flash`, critic `glm-5.3-flash`). Before: 6 runs per card, 276 runs. After: one run per card, 46 runs. The final line counts only the first run of each card; two more cards were rerun and are listed in the version table.

**Limit.** The final reruns have one run per item or card, so most per-case numbers are single runs. The gain shows in the pooled numbers; "no case got worse" holds on the evidence there is, with little margin. The run stopped because the budget was used up (198 of about 200 runs in the widened scope).
**Merged.** The code is on branch `MiquelGomezCorral/tp-critic-clues`, on base `45c6747`: commit `3fb0ce0`, merged as `114e5b3`.

**Later fix.** The `Redundant` clue picked a different clause when the same clauses came in another order, and could name a stated rule instead of the extra `Existence`. Fixed in `600d6a0`, merged as `6606ab7`; see the section before the evidence.

rows: `R4 hard Existence(has_key): has_key happens at least once; owed from the start until it is met; hard: still owed when the episode ends = failed.` One line per clause, with what breaks it for good.

Swapped `Precedence` and `Response` arguments flagged 51% to 96% (b0 to y1). With "match every line to a task phrase" (y2) extra clauses 17/84 to 28/84, at the price of rejecting the right carry set r08 every time.
`R4 Existence(has_key) is already implied by the other hard rules: every run they accept keeps it, so the machine accepts the same runs without it.`
Redundant clauses flagged 0% to 72% (b0 to y1), but only with the wording "it is a defect on its own: reject" (next section).
`Every way to finish includes: has_key, door_open, at_goal.` Computed from the machine.
Noise at first (p2). With the v3 guide ("a listed event is already required, so no `Existence` for it") it caught missing goals that v1 and v2 missed (s06, w03, w08) and made the chain form pass.
A lasting trigger is owed again
One sentence in the guide: a `Response(a, b)` with a lasting `a` needs `b` on the last step.
Not measured with margin: r05 and W1a rest on 2 runs.

blocks.title: The wording mattered more than the content
blocks.text: The same redundant fact, worded two ways in the guide. "Ask to drop it" flagged **0 of 18** redundant defects (q1, 6 reps). "It is a defect on its own: reject and ask to drop it" flagged **10 of 18** (r1) and **14 of 18** (y1), and 26 of 36 (72%) over 12 reps, where no clues flagged 0 of 36. On this small model a clue only counts if the guide says what verdict it carries.

sections.title: Two examples

items.alt: Reward Machine of item w18, a doorkey candidate with one redundant Existence
items.caption:
**w18, a redundant clause** · 5 states · final u4 · well u2
Task: *Use the key to open the door, then reach the goal.* Candidate: 4 hard clauses; `Existence(has_key)` adds nothing. Flagged with no clues 0 of 12, with plain + redundant clues (y1) 8 of 12, with the later main prompt alone (k0) 6 of 6, with v3 full 1 of 1.

details.title: Task, clauses, LTLf, clue block and RM text
details.text: The critic rejected on call 1 ("The hard `Existence(has_key)` is redundant ... Remove it") and accepted the three-clause set on call 2.
details.code:
# Task (NL)
Use the key to open the door, then reach the goal.

# Candidate clauses, all hard (item w18: a wrong candidate, one clause too many)
Existence(at_goal)
Precedence(door_open, at_goal)
Precedence(has_key, door_open)
Existence(has_key)

# LTLf, one per clause (check/example_ltlf.py)
Existence(at_goal):             (Fat_goal)
Precedence(door_open, at_goal): (((~at_goal)Udoor_open)|(G(~at_goal)))
Precedence(has_key, door_open): (((~door_open)Uhas_key)|(G(~door_open)))
Existence(has_key):             (Fhas_key)

# What the compiler added to the critic's prompt (version v3 full, run w18-r1)
## Compiler clues (computed from the clauses by the compiler, exact)

Rules in plain words:
- R1 hard Existence(at_goal): at_goal happens at least once; owed from the start until it is met; hard: still owed when the episode ends = failed.
- R2 hard Precedence(door_open, at_goal): at_goal may not happen before the first door_open; broken for good by: at_goal; a hard break fails the episode.
- R3 hard Precedence(has_key, door_open): door_open may not happen before the first has_key; broken for good by: door_open; a hard break fails the episode.
- R4 hard Existence(has_key): has_key happens at least once; owed from the start until it is met; hard: still owed when the episode ends = failed.
Redundant: R4 Existence(has_key) is already implied by the other hard rules: every run they accept keeps it, so the machine accepts the same runs without it.
Every way to finish includes: has_key, door_open, at_goal.

items: **Extra, template and event defects.** Extra clauses (w10, w15, w16), wrong templates (w01, w02, w11, w14, w22) and wrong events (w04, w05, w09) stay accepted in the baseline, y1 and every later version. Items w02, w04, w16 and w22 were flagged in none of the b0, y1, y2, k0 or v3 runs. The critic quotes the clue ("the chain also forces has_key and door_open") without checking it against the task. Untried: a per-clause quote check in the output, which needs a schema change.

**Fewer extra clauses caught.** Every clue variant that has the redundant clue catches fewer extra clauses than no clues (y1 20%, b0 33%). The task-phrase line (y2) wins them back but rejects the right carry set r08.
**Verdict before reasoning.** 2 to 7% of verdicts contradict their own text (r03, r08, S3). The schema asks for `accepted` before `feedback`; putting `feedback` first is a small change, untested.
**The generator ignores "remove".** On S2 it keeps a redundant `Existence` for 1 or 2 rounds after the critic asks to drop it (runs of 8 and 5 rounds). That is generator-side, outside the clues.
**Thin per-case evidence.** v5 rests on 2 runs for r05 and W1a; S1, U5 and U6 on 3. A confirm round of about 15 runs was planned and not run.

sections.title: Later fix: the redundant clue no longer depends on clause order
sections.intro: Found by an independent review of the merged clues, fixed on 2026-11-20. Same clauses, different order, different `Redundant` line, and the critic acts on that line.

blocks.text: Task: *Go to the goal. If you reach the goal, you must also have picked up the key at some point.* Candidate, all hard: `Existence(at_goal)`, `Existence(has_key)`, `RespondedExistence(at_goal, has_key)`. The right set drops `Existence(has_key)`: the goal and the "if" rule already force the key. With the goal hard, each of the other two clauses implies the other, so the compiler can truthfully call either one redundant. The old search tried the clauses from last to first and named the first implied one. In this order that was the `RespondedExistence`, a rule the task states, which the critic must keep. The critic rejects only on a redundant listed `Existence`, so it had no clue to remove the extra one.

blocks.heading: The clue block the critic reads, goal, key, rule
blocks.text: Only the `Redundant` line changes. The fix tries the `Existence` and `ExistenceTwo` clauses first (still last to first), then the rest. An implied listed `Existence` is now named before any other clause, as the decision record asks: a stated order or "if" rule stays.

# Before (main before 600d6a0, evidence/clues-fix/dry-main.json)
## Compiler clues (computed from the clauses by the compiler, exact)

Rules in plain words:
- R1 hard Existence(at_goal): at_goal happens at least once; owed from the start until it is met; hard: still owed when the episode ends = failed.
- R2 hard Existence(has_key): has_key happens at least once; owed from the start until it is met; hard: still owed when the episode ends = failed.
- R3 hard RespondedExistence(at_goal, has_key): if at_goal happens, has_key happens too, before or after; owed after: at_goal; hard: still owed when the episode ends = failed.
Redundant: R3 RespondedExistence(at_goal, has_key) is already implied by the other hard rules: every run they accept keeps it, so the machine accepts the same runs without it.
Every way to finish includes: at_goal, has_key.

# After (evidence/clues-fix/dry.json; check/clue_order.py prints the same with today's code)
## Compiler clues (computed from the clauses by the compiler, exact)

Rules in plain words:
- R1 hard Existence(at_goal): at_goal happens at least once; owed from the start until it is met; hard: still owed when the episode ends = failed.
- R2 hard Existence(has_key): has_key happens at least once; owed from the start until it is met; hard: still owed when the episode ends = failed.
- R3 hard RespondedExistence(at_goal, has_key): if at_goal happens, has_key happens too, before or after; owed after: at_goal; hard: still owed when the episode ends = failed.
Redundant: R2 Existence(has_key) is already implied by the other hard rules: every run they accept keeps it, so the machine accepts the same runs without it.
Every way to finish includes: at_goal, has_key.

items: **Live check.** The `glm-5.3-flash` critic on the fixed clue block, 3 runs at `none` and 3 at `high`: 6 of 6 reject and ask to remove `Existence(has_key)`. One critic call each. No live run on the old block: its clue named the clause the critic must keep, and the dry run shows it.

**Brute force: 0 mismatches.** The review's checker compares every clue line with the LTLf meaning over all valuations, on random clause sets. On main after the fix (`6606ab7`): 496 sets right, 0 wrong, 104 skipped (the machine build or the clues raise on that set); sets built to split into several hard groups: 129 right, 0 wrong, 21 skipped. The review's run before the fix gave 482, 0, 118 and 129, 0, 21. No false clue either way: both picks are true statements, and the bug was which one was named.

**Same commit.** Smaller changes from the review: the start-state check and the group split now refuse or skip clause shapes they cannot handle, a soft clause that can only be owed says "still owed when the episode ends costs a penalty", and the critic prompt says "accepts the same runs without it", the clue's own words. The unit suite has one new regression test for the order case.

**`evidence/runs/<label>.json`.** One file per label: every critic-set run without the critic's full prompt (the ablations other than y1 and the versions also lack the feedback text). `evidence/examples/` keeps the two worked examples whole, prompt included. The big `_work` folders of the original runs are not copied.

**`evidence/loop/<version>/today/`.** The pipeline-loop run records of v0 to v5, as written by the loop. `evidence/items.json` is the critic set, `evidence/guides/` the guide texts of each variant, `evidence/final.diff` the code change.
**Rescore the critic set (no model call).** `python check/rescore.py k0 v3f` prints the tables of `check/score.py`, the original scorer. The headline 30% and 56% come from this.

**Rescore the pipeline (no model call).** From the repository root, with the Conda environment `RM_RL_env`: `D=docs/paper/critic-clues/evidence/loop; CC_ROOT=$PWD PYTHONPATH=app python $D/tools/chain_score.py v0=$D/v0/today v3f=$D/v3f/today`. It reads the repository's task cards and `src.benchmark.rm_facts`, so the numbers can move if the cards change. The headline 77% and 85% come from this: `v3f` holds 50 runs, the 46 first runs (39 right, 85%) and two reruns each of U5 and U6 (43 of 50 right pooled, 86%).

**Rerun the models.** The runner scripts that called OpenCode Go (critic `glm-5.3-flash`, judge and generator `deepseek-v4.1-flash`) were prototypes of what the merged code does (`app/src/compiler/critic_clues.py` at commit `3fb0ce0`), so they are not kept. Their run records are in `evidence/runs/` and `evidence/loop/`.

**`evidence/clues-fix/`.** The order fix: the clue block before (`dry-main.json`) and after (`dry.json`), the six live critic runs (`none-r1..3`, `high-r1..3`; the `prompt` field, about 34 KB each, was removed), and the brute-force outputs before the fix (`review-before-fix-*.out`) and on main `6606ab7` (`main-6606ab7-*.out`). `python check/clue_order.py` (with `PYTHONPATH=app`) prints the clue block for both orders with today's code. The brute-force checker and the live-run tool stay in `.git/agent-memory/plans/farm-final-20261119/` (`clues-review/`, `clues-fix/`): they are review prototypes, not kept to the repository's lint rules, and the live tool calls the model.
**Code.** Commit `3fb0ce0`, merged as `114e5b3` (`app/src/compiler/critic_clues.py` and the prompt changes; the diff is `evidence/final.diff`). Base `45c6747`.
